title: Synthesis of Compact Flow-based Computing Circuits from Boolean Expressions
problem: Mapping Boolean logic onto flow-based computing circuits has been constrained by reliance on binary decision diagrams (BDDs), which results in high area overhead. The challenge is to efficiently synthesize compact circuits for executing Boolean logic within nanoscale memory arrays.
motivation: Processing in-memory using flow-based computing can accelerate high-data-rate applications beyond the limits of modern hardware by leveraging natural current flow in nanoscale memory arrays.
method: The FACTOR framework builds Boolean connectivity graphs (BCGs—diagrams showing how Boolean logic decisions interconnect) instead of binary decision diagrams (BDDs) to map logic functions onto flow-based circuits (circuits that execute logic as data flows through gates). It constructs these graphs using factorization (breaking logic into smaller pieces) and tree-based organization, then modifies them to fit onto crossbar hardware (arrays of tiny switches in nanoscale memory). The system applies time multiplexing—allowing different Boolean functions to share the same hardware at different time steps—to reduce the total circuit size.
key_novelty: Boolean connectivity graphs replace binary decision diagrams as the representation for mapping Boolean logic more compactly into flow-based computing circuits.
contributions: FACTOR framework for mapping logic functions into dense flow-based computing circuits
Introduction of Boolean connectivity graphs (BCGs) as a more versatile representation than BDDs
Methodology for constructing concise BCGs using factorization and expression trees
Time multiplexing strategy for sharing hardware between different Boolean functions
limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the paper abstract.
